Maps, nearby mosques and offline areas

On this page
  • The Qibla map
  • Nearby mosques
  • Offline areas

The Qibla map shows the Qibla line from your place to the Kaaba on a street map. From it you can also list the mosques near you, get directions to one, and download map areas to use without a connection.

Nearby mosques, directions and offline areas are in the apps for Android, iPhone, iPad, Windows, macOS and Linux. The web version shows the map and the Qibla line only.

The Qibla map

To open it, tap Qibla locator on the home screen, then Map.

The map draws:

  • the Qibla line, along the shortest path to the Kaaba;
  • the directions of today's Sunrise and Sunset from your place;
  • on a phone with a compass, a wedge showing the way the phone points.

The buttons on the map:

ButtonWhat it does
+ and −Zoom in and out
My locationReads the GPS and moves the map there; the bar under the map then offers that point as your place
Whole lineShows the whole Qibla line, from your place to Makkah
North upTurns the map back with north at the top
SatelliteShows satellite pictures instead of the street map (online only)
Follow compassTurns the map with the phone
Pick a locationTap the map to choose a new place for the app
Offline areasOpens the panel for downloading map areas
Nearby mosquesOpens the list of mosques around your place

When there is no connection and the area is not saved, Taqwim says "No connection: the street map is not available" and draws its own built-in world map with borders and names. The Qibla line is always drawn.

Nearby mosques

  1. Open the Qibla map and tap Nearby mosques.
  2. Taqwim shows Looking for mosques…, then lists the mosques around your place, nearest first. Each row gives the name, the distance and the direction. A mosque without a name in the map data is named after the nearest street.
  3. Tap a mosque in the list, or its mark on the map, to choose it.

The mosques come from OpenStreetMap's map data. If the list says "Some street data here is not available offline, so the list may be incomplete", go online or save the area at full detail (see Offline areas).

Directions

When you choose a mosque, Taqwim works out the way there by itself, from the street data:

  1. Choose By car or Walking.
  2. Read the summary (distance and time) and the list of turns. The route is drawn on the map; the dotted parts are the short walks between the road and your place or the mosque.

"The route comes from the map data, without traffic or turn restrictions: follow the road signs." The directions are meant for short trips, such as the mosques around you.

You can also hand the trip to another app: Open in Google Maps, or Open in Waze (by car only). Only the mosque's position is passed to that app.

Guidance on the way

  1. After choosing a mosque and a travel mode, tap Start.
  2. Taqwim waits for your position ("Waiting for your location…"), then follows you: the map turns with the route, and a banner shows the next turn, the distance to it, and the distance and time left.
  3. If you leave the route, Taqwim finds a new one ("Finding a new route…").
  4. When you arrive, Taqwim says so and stops.

While guiding:

  • End stops the guidance.
  • Re-centre appears after you move the map by hand; tap it to follow your position again.
  • Voice: on / Voice: off turns the spoken instructions on or off. The voice uses your phone's own speech engine, in the app's language. Computers show the instructions without voice.
  • The screen stays on. "Guidance runs while Taqwim is on screen, and knows no traffic." It stops if you leave the app.

Add a mosque the map lacks

  1. In the Nearby mosques panel, tap Add a mosque. A cross appears in the middle of the map.
  2. "Move the map until the mosque is under the cross, then save." You can also press and hold the map at the mosque's place.
  3. Type its name in Mosque name (optional).
  4. Tap Save here, or Cancel.

Your mosques are listed with the others and marked Added by you. To remove one, tap Delete, then Confirm delete. You can add up to 50 mosques. They are kept only on your device, and the backup file keeps them too.

Using the internet for street data

At the bottom of the panel, Use the internet for street data (mosques and directions) is on by default. When it is off, the mosques and the directions use only your saved areas and the street data already kept on the device.

Offline areas

Save the map of an area, such as your city, to see the street map, the mosques and the directions without a connection.

  1. Open the Qibla map and tap Offline areas. The map moves to your place; move it if you want another area.
  2. Under Download an area for offline use, the area is Around the map's centre. Choose a radius: 5, 10, 15 or 25 km.
  3. Read the plan: the expected size in megabytes and the number of map pieces (tiles), the level of detail, and the Free space on the device.
  4. Tap Download. The progress shows the pieces and megabytes so far; Cancel stops it.
  5. When it ends, Taqwim says "Area saved" with its name and size.

The level of detail:

  • full detail: every street and mosque. Needed for the nearby mosques and directions offline.
  • less detail and little detail: used when the area is larger than one download allows at full detail. Not every street or mosque shows, and the mosques and directions cannot use it offline. For full detail, choose a smaller radius; you can download several areas.

One download is at most 3,000 pieces or 50 MB. If the area is too large, Taqwim says "This area is larger than one download allows; choose a smaller radius". If the device lacks space, it says "Not enough free space for this area".

Under Saved areas, each area shows its size and a Delete button.

The maps come from OpenFreeMap, made from OpenStreetMap data. The satellite layer is never saved and needs a connection.
